title: Bittensor Daily News: November 25, 2026

updates.headline: SN24 ms.computer hosts Gambit, a playable browser chess application
updates.summary:
Gambit, a chess application hosted on SN24 ms.computer, was shared in the subnet's Bittensor Discord channel on November 24. Its public site offers play against Stockfish at eight difficulty levels and advertises play with a friend through a link. No account was required for our browser test.

We opened the application, moved a pawn to e4 and received the computer's c5 reply. The site explains that Stockfish runs on the player's device, so this is evidence of a usable hosted application, not proof that the subnet performs the chess engine's inference.

The creator's description also covers coaching, hints and a multiplayer relay. We did not test multiplayer reliability or audit the relay's encryption. The bounded test confirms an accessible application and a completed computer response; it does not establish customer numbers or revenue.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars: a working application demonstrates bounded platform use beyond a landing page. Four would overstate a single chess application as a major platform launch or adoption milestone.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Three stars: a working application demonstrates bounded platform use beyond a landing page. Four would overstate a single chess application as a major platform launch or adoption milestone.
ratingAssessment.evidence: Public application and a browser move followed by a computer response; original channel post.
ratingAssessment.scope: Single-player initial move; no account or paid interaction.
ratingAssessment.uncertainty: Multiplayer, encryption, scale and revenue not independently verified.
ratingAssessment.adjacentRatingReason: Three stars: a working application demonstrates bounded platform use beyond a landing page. Four would overstate a single chess application as a major platform launch or adoption milestone.

updates.headline: SN44 Score demonstrates yuBot with services from eight Bittensor subnets
updates.summary:
SN44 Score published its first yuBot demo on November 25, describing an open-source, private-by-default assistant and opening a waitlist. The team says its backend already connects inference from SN28 SayGM, SN64 Chutes and SN53 engy; bot computers from SN94 Cathedral and SN4 Targon; compute from SN51 lium; search from SN22 Desearch; and experts from Score itself.

The announcement describes a marketplace in which services or experts can be hired directly or reached through a user's main bot. Score plans to make this a significant part of its incentive mechanism while retaining research work on vision and world models.

This is a demonstrated product and team-reported integration announcement. It does not establish general availability, paid customer usage or an executed new emission split. The attached full demo and end-to-end service delivery remain outside this initial review.
updates.ratingReason: Four stars: a substantive assistant and multi-subnet service integration exceed a routine model-catalog addition. Five is not established by a first demo and waitlist.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Four stars: a substantive assistant and multi-subnet service integration exceed a routine model-catalog addition. Five is not established by a first demo and waitlist.
ratingAssessment.uncertainty: Full video, end-to-end delivery and paid usage not independently reviewed.
ratingAssessment.adjacentRatingReason: Four stars: a substantive assistant and multi-subnet service integration exceed a routine model-catalog addition. Five is not established by a first demo and waitlist.

updates.headline: SN66 Conjectures reports a proof-checked TorchLean optimization result
updates.summary:
In a November 19 competition result reviewed here as a dated catch-up, SN66 Conjectures reports reducing a TorchLean model workload from 16.1 milliseconds to 117 microseconds on a typical x86 setup, a roughly 137-fold speedup.

The team says Lean proofs check bit-for-bit agreement with the specification for all inputs. It reports 226 submissions across 19 operators, with 221 passing the proof gate and 150 leaderboard changes. The result concerns the stated model workload and competition, not all AI inference. We have not independently rerun the benchmark or audited the proofs.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars: a concrete measured competition result warrants operational coverage. The standing competition cap prevents promotion to four based on the speedup alone.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Three stars: a concrete measured competition result warrants operational coverage. The standing competition cap prevents promotion to four based on the speedup alone.
ratingAssessment.uncertainty: Benchmark and proof artifacts not independently executed.
ratingAssessment.adjacentRatingReason: Three stars: a concrete measured competition result warrants operational coverage. The standing competition cap prevents promotion to four based on the speedup alone.

updates.headline: SN75 Hippius reports faster writes in a defined mounted-bucket test
updates.summary:
SN75 Hippius published a storage comparison on November 25 using rsync to copy a folder into an s3fs-mounted bucket. With the same client and settings, the team reports 681 milliseconds per file for Hippius, versus 2,503 for Cloudflare R2 and 5,678 for Backblaze B2.

That is roughly 3.7 and 8.3 times faster in this specific test. It is not a result for every storage workload, geography or file size. The figures are team-reported and have not been independently reproduced in this review.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars: a specified operational comparison is useful beyond promotion. Four would overstate a single self-reported workload as a broader product breakthrough.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Three stars: a specified operational comparison is useful beyond promotion. Four would overstate a single self-reported workload as a broader product breakthrough.
ratingAssessment.uncertainty: Independent reproduction and broader workload coverage not established.
ratingAssessment.adjacentRatingReason: Three stars: a specified operational comparison is useful beyond promotion. Four would overstate a single self-reported workload as a broader product breakthrough.

updates.headline: SN80 OpenRoboto reports a 50,000-hour robotics-data agreement
updates.summary:
SN80 OpenRoboto says it has signed an agreement to collect 50,000 hours of first-person robotics data for an unnamed robotics lab. Its November 24 article describes collection in commercial and industrial environments, with the team coordinating customer requirements, quality and delivery. OpenTensor highlighted the announcement on November 25.

The team says miner rewards are being aligned with accepted data. It plans to reinvest most funds and use part of profits for staking rewards and periodic buybacks. Those are the announced arrangements, not guaranteed holder returns.

The contract's monetary value, customer identity and collected revenue were not disclosed in the reviewed announcement. Fifty thousand hours is the agreement's scope, not evidence that all footage has already been delivered. Gamma activity and credit creation are separate from proof of customer revenue.
updates.ratingReason: Four stars: a defined commercial data-collection agreement is substantive adoption news beyond routine availability. Five is not established by the disclosed scope and delivery evidence.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Four stars: a defined commercial data-collection agreement is substantive adoption news beyond routine availability. Five is not established by the disclosed scope and delivery evidence.
ratingAssessment.evidence: SN80 OpenRoboto agreement article, November 24; OpenTensor follow-up, November 25
ratingAssessment.scope: Original team article and OpenTensor follow-up.
ratingAssessment.uncertainty: Customer unnamed; price, collected revenue and complete delivery not independently established.
ratingAssessment.adjacentRatingReason: Four stars: a defined commercial data-collection agreement is substantive adoption news beyond routine availability. Five is not established by the disclosed scope and delivery evidence.

updates.headline: SN81 Reliquary publishes a method for distributed model-training corrections
updates.summary:
SN81 Reliquary's Gumbel Substitution research describes correcting differences between distributed model samplers and a training model using shared random noise. Its paper was submitted November 20 and highlighted by the team on November 24.

The authors report post-training a nine-billion-parameter model over 11 days and 15.75 billion tokens, using 161 sampler accounts across more than 11 GPU types. They report substituting 1.21% of tokens and improvements on eight held-out benchmarks. These are the authors' measurements, not an independently replicated result.

The method's guarantees depend on its protocol assumptions. The production run lacked an otherwise identical uncorrected run; controlled comparisons were separate laboratory experiments. The work is a substantive attempt to make heterogeneous distributed training reliable, not proof that arbitrary untrusted training is solved.
updates.ratingReason: Four stars: a concrete method and substantial distributed training experiment exceed routine benchmark commentary. Five is not established as a general solution by the bounded experimental evidence.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Four stars: a concrete method and substantial distributed training experiment exceed routine benchmark commentary. Five is not established as a general solution by the bounded experimental evidence.
ratingAssessment.evidence: Gumbel Substitution paper, November 20; Reliquary research explanation; SN81 Reliquary research announcement, November 24
ratingAssessment.scope: Original paper abstract, research blog and team announcement.
ratingAssessment.uncertainty: Full paper and independent replication remain pending; production comparison lacks an uncorrected twin.
ratingAssessment.adjacentRatingReason: Four stars: a concrete method and substantial distributed training experiment exceed routine benchmark commentary. Five is not established as a general solution by the bounded experimental evidence.

updates.headline: SN124 Swarm wins Andorra funding for autonomous ski-resort inspections
updates.summary:
SN124 Swarm announced on November 24 that its Snowline project has secured an Andorran government research grant. The government's November 10 award notice lists EUR 95,314.67 for the project, independently supporting the team's funding announcement.

Snowline combines docked autonomous drones with optical and thermal inspection to monitor ski-resort infrastructure, including lifts, snowmaking equipment and slope protection. The team also describes support for searches for missing people.

Swarm plans a 12-month testing program. The news is funded development and testing, not proof of a completed commercial deployment or demonstrated search-and-rescue performance. The government's award predates the team's latest announcement; it was not newly granted today.
updates.ratingReason: Four stars: independently documented government funding for a defined real-world deployment trial exceeds routine project promotion. Five is not established by a funded trial whose operational results remain ahead.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Four stars: independently documented government funding for a defined real-world deployment trial exceeds routine project promotion. Five is not established by a funded trial whose operational results remain ahead.

ratingAssessment.scope: Government award notice and November 24 team announcement.
ratingAssessment.uncertainty: Trial delivery and commercial rollout remain unverified.
ratingAssessment.adjacentRatingReason: Four stars: independently documented government funding for a defined real-world deployment trial exceeds routine project promotion. Five is not established by a funded trial whose operational results remain ahead.

ecosystem.headline: Runtime 495 expands configurable mechanisms and changes new Gamma deposits
ecosystem.summary:
Subtensor runtime 495 was released on November 24 and is running on Finney in our November 25 finalized-chain checks. The release changes the Null-consensus UID budget to 2,500, independent of mechanism count.

The default global mechanism limit remains two. Root can raise it to a hard maximum of 16; the change does not mean every subnet already has 16 mechanisms. The per-mechanism row limit divides the 2,500 budget by mechanism count. Yuma's existing 256-product bound is unchanged.

New owner-funded Gamma emission deposits open without a daily spending cap instead of starting with a zero cap. Existing deposits are unaffected. The release also changes root-claim weight accounting. These are deployed capabilities and defaults, not evidence that every subnet has adopted them; the precise activation block was not established in this targeted review.
ecosystem.ratingReason: Four stars: deployed network capabilities and Gamma defaults affect subnet operators beyond routine maintenance. Five is not established by these bounded protocol changes.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Four stars: deployed network capabilities and Gamma defaults affect subnet operators beyond routine maintenance. Five is not established by these bounded protocol changes.
ratingAssessment.evidence: Subtensor runtime 495 release; Runtime 495 implementation; Finalized runtime review evidence
ratingAssessment.scope: Official release, merged implementation and finalized runtime 495 snapshot.
ratingAssessment.uncertainty: Exact activation block and individual subnet feature adoption not established.
ratingAssessment.adjacentRatingReason: Four stars: deployed network capabilities and Gamma defaults affect subnet operators beyond routine maintenance. Five is not established by these bounded protocol changes.

ecosystem.headline: Yuma researches a feedback-based approach to subnet liquidity
ecosystem.summary:
Yuma published Alpha Subnet Market Reloaded, or ASMR, on November 24. Researcher Youssef El Moujahid proposes tying pool operations to measured trading flow and liquidity depth. This is research, not an approved or implemented Bittensor upgrade. The papers explicitly retain the emission-allocation rule; ASMR changes liquidity management, which can indirectly affect prices and emission shares.

The papers explore releasing TAO and alpha proportionally, retiring protocol-injected alpha and retaining earned alpha in a vault. Returned TAO could remain in its pool, move to other pools or stay in a vault under different modeled policies. The distinction matters: the proposal does not simply burn every holder's earned tokens.

Yuma reports that liquidity in ten liquid pools rose 196% while trading fell 61% between June 2025 and September 30, 2026. Its simulations freeze a September 30 network configuration and omit factors including profit-taking, front-running and future parameter changes. Modeled outcomes are not forecasts. Full technical-paper review remains ongoing; the initial report covers the published summary and specified mechanism descriptions.
ecosystem.ratingReason: Four stars: original market measurements and a specified alternative emission mechanism have substantial reader consequences beyond a fund opinion. Five is not established by simulations without protocol adoption.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Four stars: original market measurements and a specified alternative emission mechanism have substantial reader consequences beyond a fund opinion. Five is not established by simulations without protocol adoption.
ratingAssessment.evidence: Yuma ASMR announcement, November 24; Yuma ASMR research summary; Yuma ASMR mechanism research
ratingAssessment.scope: Yuma summary and linked foundational and mechanism papers.
ratingAssessment.uncertainty: Full technical review unfinished; simulation assumptions limit predictions; no adoption asserted.
ratingAssessment.adjacentRatingReason: Four stars: original market measurements and a specified alternative emission mechanism have substantial reader consequences beyond a fund opinion. Five is not established by simulations without protocol adoption.
